verifier_own.text:
MY OWN RESULT (steps 7 and 8, as I could re-derive and inspect them)

A. ACS B19013 (Indiana, U.S.), 2015 to 2023: I could NOT independently re-fetch any value.
- Step 1 to step 5 report every ACS value as UNAVAILABLE, because the Census API returned "Missing Key" [S8][S13][S17][S31][S53][S58]. My own web searches (2015 Indiana, 2015 U.S.) returned no readable B19013 figure either. I do not fill values from memory.
- So the nominal values, the adjusted values and all four percentage changes (Indiana and U.S., nominal and real) cannot be computed or verified. The correct result for steps 7 and 8, given the inputs, is "adjusted values not computable".

B. CPI-U CUUR0000SA0 annual average (M13), index 1982-84=100
- Claimed in step 6 (BLS API v2, fetched 2026-10-23) [S59][S63]: 2015 237.017; 2016 240.007; 2017 245.120; 2018 251.107; 2019 255.657; 2020 258.811; 2021 270.970; 2022 292.655; 2023 304.702.
- My check: the CSV holds these same CPI values [S85]. The saved API text shows 2018 M13 Annual = 251.107 [S84]. A saved 2015 source row ends in 237.017, which is consistent with the 2015 annual average [S85]. My search for 2015/2019/2023 gave no independent page I could read, so only 2015 and 2018 are cross-checked against raw saved text. The other seven values rest on step 6's own extraction [S63].
- The CPI deflators I computed (CPI_2023 / CPI_year) are:
  - 2015: 304.702 / 237.017 = 1.28557
  - 2016: 304.702 / 240.007 = 1.26955
  - 2017: 304.702 / 245.120 = 1.24301
  - 2018: 304.702 / 251.107 = 1.21340
  - 2019: 304.702 / 255.657 = 1.19184
  - 2020: 304.702 / 258.811 = 1.17728
  - 2021: 304.702 / 270.970 = 1.12449
  - 2022: 304.702 / 292.655 = 1.04117
  - 2023: 1.00000
- The CPI-only price rise from 2015 to 2023 is 304.702 / 237.017 − 1 = 28.56%.
- Adjusted_2023 = nominal x deflator. Because no nominal values exist, no adjusted value can be checked.

C. Step 7 file check (income_cpi_adjusted.csv), from Bash [S84][S85]
- The file exists. Its header has the 12 required columns: year, geography, acs_nominal_usd, acs_moe_usd, cpi_u_annual_avg, adjusted_2023_usd, nominal_pct_change_2015_2023, real_pct_change_2015_2023, note, acs_source_url, cpi_source_url, retrieved_date [S84].
- There are 18 year rows (2015 to 2023, two geographies each) plus 2 summary rows, which makes 20 data rows [S85].
- The acs_nominal_usd, adjusted_2023_usd and percent-change columns are empty in every row. The note column says "ACS value UNAVAILABLE (Census API returned Missing Key; not filled)" [S84][S85].
- The 2020 rows are flagged "EXPERIMENTAL: no standard 2020 ACS 1-year release" [S85].
- The retrieved_date is 2026-10-23 on every row [S85]. The ACS URL columns carry the API endpoint URLs and the CPI URL column carries the BLS API URL [S84].
- The summary rows say the percent changes are "not computable" [S85].
- The "adjusted 2023 value equals the 2023 nominal value" criterion cannot be met, because there is no nominal value.

D. Step 8 PNG check
- real_income_indiana_vs_us.png exists. Its size is 1800 x 1050 px [S85], which meets the ≥1000 px width criterion.
- chart.py contains read_csv / savefig / hatch / dpi patterns. My grep output was cut, so I did not confirm the chart's title, legend and footnote text. I did not view the image.
- Because the CSV has no income values, a bar chart of real income cannot plot real data. What the PNG actually shows is UNVERIFIED. It may be empty or a placeholder.

E. Cannot confirm
- All ACS B19013 values (no key, no readable data.census.gov table).
